title: Titans' Tony Pollard got extra motivation during the offseason
description: Tennessee Titans' Tony Pollard feels like an underdog after offseason chatter and is motivated to prove himself in 2026.
fullText:
For most of the offseason, the Tennessee Titans' focus has been on building around quarterback Cam Ward.

Everything from head coach Robert Saleh hiring Brian Daboll as offensive coordinator to bringing in Wan'Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate was made to help Ward develop in year two. But one weapon who can be an asset to Ward in 2026 often gets overlooked: Tony Pollard.

In fact, in April, a large portion of the fanbase was ready to move on from Pollard, calling on the organization to draft Notre Dame running back Jeremiyah Love. While the Arizona Cardinals eventually prevented that from happening, Pollard told Tyler Dunne of Go Long that he got the message loud and clear and now has something to prove in what could be his final season in Nashville.

"It all put me back into the prime spot to feel like I'm the underdog," Pollard says. "I'm easily overlooked. So it's easy for me to get up and get going. It's easy for me to grind and give my all every day because I know they might not be expecting that from me, or they may be surprised by the things that I'm doing. I look at it as motivation."

Pollard ran hard in training camp and looked the part of the Titans' feature back behind an offensive line that looked good as run blockers. If he can continue to build upon that once the season starts, his emergence could set the Titans' offense for success, and who knows, maybe a couple more seasons in Nashville.

title: Chelsea lineup today vs Arsenal: Who will start in London Derby?

The Premier League season has just started, but already Chelsea has a high-stakes match that will put its perfect start to the test, making a short trip to north London to face Arsenal.

The Xabi Alonso era started with two victories, with the Blues beating Fulham and Brighton & Hove Albion, but both of those wins showed some flaws. Chelsea conceded two in the first game and three in the second, even with Argentina No. 1 Dibu Martinez, who arrived from Aston Villa this summer, making four saves.

Signing the goalkeeper and his former Aston Villa teammate Morgan Rogers meant lots of Chelsea's business already was done by the time deadline day came this week, though they did send Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in a record deal and also tried to bring in Lamine Camara from Monaco to replace him in the middle only to see that deal fall apart at the last minute.

title: How Tennessee football's Mike Matthews is setting stage for return home
description: Wide receiver Mike Matthews set personal highs with 132 yards and two touchdowns from Faizon Brandon in Tennessee football's season opener.
fullText:
Mike Matthews opened the 2026 season for Tennessee football with a bang, setting personal single-game highs with 132 receiving yards and two touchdowns in the 56-9 win over Furman at Neyland Stadium on Sept. 5.

The outing has the junior wide receiver soaring into Week 2, when the No. 18 Vols (1-0) play Georgia Tech (0-1) at Bobby Dodd Stadium in Atlanta, just 22 miles from his hometown of Lilburn.

"It's a pretty good confidence-builder, but I've been working hard all offseason," Matthews said. "I kind of knew that my heart is going to show when I play on the field, so I try to play with heart. God put me in a good position and it played out the right way."

Matthews enjoyed a breakout season for the Vols in 2025, setting career highs for receptions (32), yards (813) and touchdowns (four). Entering 2026, he's catching passes from his third different starting quarterback in as many years.

It was the first game he played with five-star freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon, but they clearly have developed a quick and easy connection.

Matthews' two touchdown receptions went for 55 and 57 yards. The first came on a busted coverage from Furman, when Brandon's running ability drew a safety up enough for Matthews to run free behind the defense. Matthews had to fight through contact to haul in the second score.

"It was just like practice," Matthews said. "A lot of our deep balls have just been on point every time, so it was nothing I wasn't used to."

Matthews was happy about the win to start the season, but immediately after beating Furman, his attention turned to Georgia Tech.

"It just fills me up, makes me proud," he said about playing close to home. "But coming up, I know I got to lock in for next week, get ready for the game, prepare and just be who I am."

title: Refs, Bryce Underwood big losers in Michigan's miracle win vs WMU
description: Andrew Birkle picks the winners and losers from Michigan football's shocking Week 1 13-12 win over Western Michigan on a Hail Mary in Ann Arbor.
fullText:
Free Press sports writer Andrew Birkle picks the winners and losers from Michigan football's shocking Week 1 13-12 win over Western Michigan on a Hail Mary in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Sept. 5, in Kyle Whittingham's first game as Michigan's coach.

How about a memory-making miracle in your first game in maize and blue?

Just absurd stuff from Buchanan, a Utah transfer touted as a big-time playmaker by Michigan's new staff, and showed what he has in his bag by hauling in Michigan's second Hail Mary attempt, after a controversial decision by the refs to save Michigan.

He finished with just six catches but gained 126 yards, boosted by his 47-yard touchdown catch with no time on the clock.

NO JOY IN ANN ARBOR? Hail Mary fuels conspiracists as Michigan football pays for its past

JJ Buchanan with a beautiful one-handed snag 👏 @UMichFootball

📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/YNyKCElan4

Michigan's defensive end factory continues to produce winners.

Nichols looks like the next productive edge rusher for the Wolverines after Derrick Moore and Jaishawn Barham departed for the NFL draft.

On Western's second drive, Nichols made a nice tackle to stuff a Broncos run, then sacked quarterback Broc Lowry to force a punt.

SHAWN WINDSOR: Michigan football had every reason to lose to WMU. But history had other ideas

That was just one sequence in a dominant first half that included five total tackles, 1½ sacks and 2½ tackles for loss.

He finished the day with nine total tackles and it looks like Michigan's got another dude on the defensive line to pair with 2025 All-American John Henry Daley when he gets more healthy.

This one will be discussed for years to come, and rightfully so.

There were literally zeroes on the clock. Michigan was the loser, Western Michigan the winner in Ann Arbor.

When the refs announced a review, it seemed like a formality. However, after a lengthy holdup, referee Jim Wharrie's crew announced – without much explanation – that there was 1 second on the clock, seemingly because the WMU defender touched the ball while out of bounds.

TV TIME: Michigan football Hail Mary winner questioned as time appeared to run out

However, NBC rules analyst Terry McAauley vehemently disagreed with the crew's decision:

"Our in-set clock is in-synch, is the actual stadium clock, the ball isn't even close to touching a player when it goes to zero," McAauley said on the NBC broadcast. "Now their system, their Hawk-eye system, apparently either had a different synch or whatever and they came up with 1 second when it touched the players. I don't see how that happened, assuming our clock is correct.

"It is clearly not touching a player, the ball is clearly still in the air when the clock goes to zero, on our screens. The Big Ten is going to have to tell a lot of us how did they get to one second on this play."

McAauley's reaction lines up with the eye test. Assuming there's not another angle, this could be an all-time blunder and one that potentially stole history from Western Michigan.

There were plenty of excuses to be made for Underwood after his first season in Ann Arbor: no designated quarterback coach, getting flung into a messy coaching situation, unrealistic expectations – and the Wolverines still went 9-4. The hope was that an offseason working under new offensive coordinator Jason Beck would correct many of the mechanical and processing issues Underwood showed as a freshman.

Outside of an impressive first drive in which he went 5-for-5 for 61 yards, another 11 yards rushing and a TD on the ground, things went about as bad as possible for Underwood.

After leading an 11-play, 75-yard drive that was capped off with a QB sneak from Underwood, Michigan went punt, punt, punt, punt, interception. And that included some lucky breaks. On Michigan's second drive, Underwood tried to play hero and squeeze in a pass down the sideline on third and long and was intercepted before it was ruled Western's defender tipped the ball while a few inches out of bounds, negating the pick. On the last drive before the half, Underwood recklessly threw a pass in the boundary that was well-read and intercepted by linebacker Dillon Moore; it easily could've been a pick-six if Moore's momentum hadn't landed him on the sideline at the 26.

As if things could get worse, Underwood barely got the ball in the second half with Western's dominant ball control, and when he did have it, things went terribly.

Michigan opened the half with two punts and then Underwood had a crushing fumble to give WMU the ball back deep in Michigan territory.

A Hail Mary connection will certainly buy him some good will, but before that, he was just 10-for-15 passing for just 95 yards with nine carries for 47 yards rushing.

There's still a lot of work to be done.

REACTIONS: Michigan fans get second lease on life after Hail Mary: 'Man I love football'

If I had to sum up this insane game for Michigan ... well, I can't really use the words in a family publication that come to mind for the plays between the first and final drives.

Michigan's first drive of the game couldn't have gone better, ending in a touchdown after 11 plays. Michigan didn't score again until the last play of the game.

Michigan committed nine penalties for 80 yards.

Michigan's offensive line was pushed around all game, forcing Underwood to play under pressure and creating no gaps for a run game that picked up just 106 yards on the ground.

Underwood reverted back to so many of the old bad habits that Michigan fans were hoping that Beck and Co. spent the offseason fixing.

Michigan's defense, which was far from the biggest problem, allowed a 20-play drive that milked nearly 14 minutes off the clock and tilted the game heavily in Western's favor.

In Nick Saban's first year at Alabama, the Crimson Tide lost to University of Louisiana-Monroe.

Whittingham and Beck were saved from a loss on that level of ignominy with a miracle catch by Buchanan, but this was far from the ideal start for Michigan, which has a lot to fix before Oklahoma comes to town next week.

One of the most frequent topics this summer on "Hail Yes!", the Free Press' Michigan football and basketball podcast, was if Marsh could be the person to break Michigan's 1,000-yard receiver drought.

The wideout was unbelievable in the second half of the season last year, finishing with 651 yards and five total touchdowns after having just one catch in the first four games.

This did not look like the start to a breakout year.

Marsh muffed a punt in the first quarter that led to a WMU field goal and finished with just two catches for 17 yards before garbage time. This game won't be remembered for Marsh's poor performance, but he left a lot to be desired.

title: Social media reacts to Nebraska's win over the Ohio Bobcats
description: Social media was buzzing after the Huskers defeated the Bobcats on Saturday afternoon.
fullText:
Nebraska football defeated the Ohio Bobcats 49-21 on Saturday. It was a tense few moments for Husker fans, as Nebraska led only 14-13 at halftime.

Nevertheless, Nebraska used a solid fourth quarter to pull away in the end. They scored 21 total points in the fourth quarter alone, giving them their first win of the season.

Freshman running back Jamal Rule made his presence felt in this game, as he had 122 rushing yards on 15 carries and two touchdowns. His 100-yard rushing game was the first by a freshman in a season opener since quarterback Adrian Martinez had 117 rushing yards against Colorado in the 2018 opener

Quarterback Anthony Colandrea completed 18-of-32 passes for 275 yards and three touchdowns in his Nebraska debut. Nebraska also had eight pass breakups in the game, its most since 2024.

Nebraska's victory marked the third straight year it has won its season opener and was the 100th victory in a season opener in program history. The Huskers are 100-32-5 all-time in season openers.

Overall, it was not a complete game, but the Huskers managed to put things together in the second half to get the job done. Social media reacted strongly to the victory, as the Huskers look ahead to Bowling Green.

title: Here is everything we learned from Texas A&M's 50-0 win over MO State
description: On Saturday, Texas A&M took on the Missouri State. Check out our top takeaways from the 50-0 shutout victory.
fullText:
No. 8 Texas A&M didn't look like the 8th-ranked team early in the first half of Saturday's season opener vs. Missouri State, as the revamped offensive line looked borderline horrific, allowing a handful of pressures and two sacks on starting quarterback Marcel Reed.

Third-year coach Mike Elko made the necessary changes that were noticeable as soon as halftime ended, while OL coach Adam Cushing also made adjustments to his rotation that produced a much better second-half performance, especially in the run game. Marcel Reed was nearly flawless, completing 21/30 for 233 yards and two touchdowns, deserving his spot on the bench late in the second half.

On the ground, WR Terry Bussey, sophomore running back Jamarion Morrow, and freshman RB Carsyn Baker scored touchdowns, led by Rueben Owens' 77 yards on 17 carries. Transfer wide receiver Isaiah Horton made his presence felt, recording a game-high 77 yards and a touchdown, continuing where he left off during the preseason.

Texas A&M's defense was elite, allowing 30 passing yards and 37 rushing yards for 67 total yards on the night, which is even more impressive after recording just one sack, while sophomore linebacker Noah Mikhail led the team with seven tackles. Right now, I fully expect the Aggie D to get even better as the season rolls on.

Earning its first shutout win since 1993, the Aggies left Kyle Field with a 50-0 victory, spurring plenty of takeaways before hosting Arizona State on Saturday. Here is everything we learned from Saturday's blowout win.

At 6'4" and 215 pounds, former Alabama wide receiver Isaiah Horton truly was the missing link to last season's productive receiver corps, but this season, Saturday's win proved that Horton was the cherry on top of what should be considered one of the deepest wide receiver rooms in the country.

Leading the game with 76 yards and his first touchdown of the season, Horton is just getting started, already becoming a favorite target for Marcel Reed on deep balls and red zone looks, while pairing well with Mario Craver, Ashton Bethel-Roman, and Terry Bussey. Expect Reed to heavily target Horton against Arizona's State on Saturday.

Texas A&M junior LB Daymion Sanford warmed up but did not play on Saturday, and based on how his fellow linebackers performed, it was a good move from Mike Elko to save his star defender for the rest of the season. Leading the game with seven tackles, sophomore LB Noah Mikhail was highly impressive, while transfer backer Ray Coney was second on the team with six tackles and half a TFL.

The combination of speed, size, and physicality, especially in the run game, helped limit Missouri State to 67 total yards, which is the lowest total allowed from an A&M defense in 30 years. Adding Sanford back into the lineup will make this unit one of the best in the SEC, especially if freshman Tamarion Watkins, who recorded two tackles and a TFL, continues to receive more playing time.

Texas A&M's offensive line was a disaster in the first half, allowing several early pressures and forcing Marcel Reed to use his legs, which was successful on nearly every attempt, but also resulted in two sacks. Junior Blake Ivy struggled during his first start at left guard, while senior center Mark Nabou committed multiple penalties.

Whatever adjustments Mike Elko and OL coach Adam Cushing made resulted in the Aggie O-line allowing zero sacks and giving Marcel Reed plenty of time to make his reads and deliver accurate throws, while opening up the running game, which produced 236 yards and three touchdowns.

The OL struggling this early is good timing for Elko and Cushing to make lineup changes, or simply fix the communication issues before hosting Arizona State, and especially before SEC play begins.

Texas A&M's run game exploded in the second half, as wide receiver Terry Bussey, sophomore running back Jamarion Morrow, and freshman back Carsyn Baker all scored touchdowns, paired with freshman KJ Edwards producing 44 yards on five carries for 8.8 yards per carry.

Rueben Owens led the room with 77 yards, but it's clear that Baker and Edwards are the most explosive options outside of Jamarion Morrow, and after the win, Mike Elko stated that both youngsters are "going to play a lot" moving forward.

With the new 5-for-5 rule taking effect this season, Mike Elko isn't just forced to play most of his freshmen, but will gladly do so if this level of play continues. Owens and Morrow will continue to lead the room, while Baker and Edwards provide elite depth.

After his best preseason performance yet, redshirt junior Marcel Reed made impressive throw after impressive throw on Saturday, showcasing his improved accuracy and touch, while layering several passes that proved his offseason was built around correcting his remaining mechanical issues.

Despite the poor O-line play in the first half, first-year OC Holmon Wiggins allowed Reed to use his legs, opening up the passing game, which led to Reed delivering red-zone strikes to Isaiah Horton and Mario Craver for his two touchdown throws before hitting the bench late in the second half, completing an efficient 21/30 for 233 yards and two touchdowns.

For the Aggies to have any legitimate shot at making it back to the College Football Playoff, Marcel Reed will need to continue elevating his game and playing with confidence in the pocket.

title: Have Liverpool Finally Unlocked Alexander Isak?
description: Liverpool seem to be onto an unexpected partnership in Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo.
fullText:
After last season's struggle for Alexander Isak to find fitness only to then suffer a broken leg, it was hard for anyone to assess whether the drawn out transfer saga and price was worth it for the highly rated Swedish striker. It perhaps didn't help Isak either that the excellent form of Hugo Ekitike, another centre forward brought in the same summer, was there as a constant and rarely flattering point of comparison.

With Hugo suffering a ruptured Achilles tendon, though, the spotlight eventually turned back to Isak. Yet in such a badly misfiring Liverpool team, it was probably too much to expect him to start banging in the goals instantly. As a result, it probably wasn't until the 2026 World Cup tournament where Liverpool supporters began to see glimpses from Isak that hinted towards why the club were so determined to get him in regardless of price.

Thankfully Isak made it through the World Cup without injury and got some much needed game minutes in his legs—and perhaps too a little confidence—for the approaching new Premier League season under Andoni Iraola's coaching. In the opening game away against Newcastle, though, it again wasn't a good team performance, and this writer struggled to see what Isak was bringing other than a target player who's movement felt more stationary than fluid while not offering much in pressing.

Singling out Isak there would be a little harsh due to the whole team not pressing with intensity nor particularly playing coherently in passing and play patterns, but it wasn't the hot start to year two everyone would have been hoping for.

With the second game against Crystal Palace at Anfield, there was hope that the players would be lifted by the home crowd. It was a game where we saw Cody Gakpo starting on the right—and thankfully, Gakpo took very well to the right, including delivering the cross which Isak turned into a goal. Even though the game showed some of the same worrying vulnerabilities in the team, it seemed like it might be a sign of better days ahead for Isak individually at least.

Then came Friday night's game against Ipswich, one that on paper looked a certain win for Liverpool. And in the end it was indeed all three points that the Reds earned, which was vital. It was also an interesting lineup chosen by Iraola with loan signing Ronald Araujo starting as right back and Jemery Frimpong on the bench whilst Gakpo was back on the left with exciting new signing Bradley Barcola watching on.

As vital as those three points were, it was also a chance to see Iraola's tactics starting to take a deeper hold on the players that encouraged this writer, as well the pregame preparation by Iraola and his coaching team. The name of the game was defensive solidity blended with the desire for Isak to be found by his teammates and it only took six minutes for it all to bear fruit with Gakpo finding Isak with a great pass who turned it into a very well taken goal.

Three minutes later and it was Gakpo again with quick thinking and a delicious pass, this time with the outside of his right foot, that found Isak. And once again Isak created his path to goal with some nice footwork and a calm finish.

After the match Iraola was asked about Isak and how to get him involved:

"Today I think we were much better in the press, especially in the first half. So we were recovering very high and then we can contact with him in good positions, No?

"If we recover the ball lower, I think it's going to be more difficult to find him.

"He will have less spaces, so it's a matter of collective effort so we can put our number nine in situations he had today."

Iraola also mentioned candidly that his biggest conversations with Isak haven't been about his scoring but what he needs to do to help the team during games, and this writer at least would say that Isak needs to work on being stronger in holding onto the ball allowing other teammates to get into counter attacking positions.

Connected to that perhaps is the concern that Isak may always be something of a luxury player in as much as he clearly considers scoring his main purpose, a little like Erling Haaland at Manchester City, and doesn't appear to seek to involve himself overmuch beyond that. For this writer, and maybe it's partly due to the love for all things Roberto Firmino (Bobby Dazzler you beauty) or a player Hugo Ekitike, that can be difficult.

For many Liverpool fans, getting involved in games and influencing them with link-up play, flicks, tricks and a certain swagger as well goals—or for when the goals aren't coming—feels a core part of a striker's job. But saying as much is an admittance of bias and preference rather than objective judgement. Most strikers, after all, don't play like Roberto Firmino. Or Hugo Ekitike.

Most importantly for now, then, and as the win against Ipswich proved, is whether Isak's teammates are finding hi, quickly before the space he has made is closed down by the opponent's defense. At the very least, we can hope to see the best possible version of Alexander Isak, and that's probably only ever going to happen with the team around him clicking.

With the Champions league getting underway this coming week and the Reds welcoming Atletico Madrid to Anfield on Wednesday evening, there is going to be a whole other level of opponent and atmosphere for new Liverpool players to experience and new head coach Andoni Iraola. It will make for a far tougher test than Ipswich. Let's hope Gakpo can find Isak again a few more times.

title: Taylor's 'dream ending to a dream career'
description: Fairytale endings in boxing are a rarity, but Irish icon Katie Taylor sails off into the sunset after the most perfect of farewells at Dublin's towering Croke Park.
fullText:
"There's nothing like an Irish family."

Katie Taylor addressed the Croke Park crowd as she paid tribute to her mother Bridget, but her extended family of 83,000 inside Croke Park and many more tuning in will have known this one was for them too.

Fairytale endings in boxing are a rarity, but Taylor is no ordinary fighter and her swansong proved as extraordinary as the fighter and person.

After 30 years lacing up the gloves, Taylor, 40, sails off into the sunset after the most perfect of farewells in front of 83,000 adoring fans at Dublin's iconic Croke Park, just three miles from the scene of her first official bout 25 years earlier.

The final act in the ring was to sweep past Flora Pili to cement her legacy in Ireland and beyond, bowing out as a three-time and two-weight undisputed champion.

It was a night of celebration, cheers and plenty of tears as fans and peers turned out for her victory lap, showing love and appreciation for a career which thrilled and inspired in equal measure.

"It was everything I expected and more," Taylor said at her final post-fight news conference.

"Thankfully I was able to hold my emotions together tonight as I was getting emotional all week and the last few months' preparation was so emotional.

"The atmosphere was so special. I was beyond my wildest dreams - what a special night."

Taylor crowns career in stylish Croke Park triumph

Tears, blood & triumph - Taylor's iconic career in pictures

Before her hand could be raised in the ring, there were battles to be won outside of it.

Born in 1986 as the youngest of four children to former Irish champion father Peter and mother Bridget - one of Ireland's first female officials - the very notion of women's boxing in Ireland appeared fanciful.

While older brothers Lee and Peter were welcomed into the boxing fold, Katie became K from Bray - a girl hiding her identity to simply compete in an exclusively male environment.

The fighting spirit and determination which characterises her sporting prowess is as much a feature of her personality, and in 2001 as a 15-year-old she took part in the first sanctioned women's bout in Ireland since it was outlawed following future world champion Deirdre Gogarty's 1991 debut in Limerick.

Perhaps fitting, as five years earlier, Taylor wrote to role model Gogarty, expressing frustration at the lack of opportunities to compete and outlining her dreams of one day being allowed to compete at the Olympic Games.

Prophetic words, as it was her exceptional talent on display in front of International Olympic Committee members in 2007 which convinced them to add women's boxing to the programme for London 2012.

All eyes were on her as Katie mania grew throughout the Games - her victory over Sofya Ochigava in the lightweight final a moment of national sporting joy comparable to the heady days of Jack Charlton's Republic of Ireland teams at the 1990 and 1994 World Cups - the Excel arena transformed into a small corner of Ireland on an unforgettable day.

A recognised star in Irish boxing circles was now a household name, her humble and gracious manner winning the hearts of a nation that has remained firmly in her corner.

"The 'ole ole oles' carried me all over the world: to Leeds, to Manchester, Brooklyn, Boston, Dallas, Manhattan," she reflected.

"This night is so special because I wanted to put on a performance for them. I don't think it was a career-best performance, but I got the win for them, just to say 'thank you'."

Her star did not dim despite a disappointing Rio Games in 2016, and while Matchroom boss Eddie Hearn took convincing to take a punt on her as a professional, the faith has been repaid in spades.

Within three years, Taylor was undisputed champion at lightweight, rising from undercard to centre stage as she carried out her promise to do for women's professional boxing what she had achieved as an amateur, all to a chorus of the aforementioned 'ole ole oles' from the support which followed her every move.

A seminal night in 2022 saw her defeat Amanda Serrano at a sold-out Madison Square Garden in a fight of the year contender - the first time a women's bout had headlined the famous arena, a major turning point for the female code.

They would trade leather a further two times after Taylor had avenged her sole professional career defeat by Chantelle Cameron to become a two-weight champion.

Perhaps that was the perfect way to sign off, but the Croke Park itch had to be scratched and while those gates seemed destined to remain locked, Taylor's status made it happen.

Could she fill such a vast stadium? Of course. Perhaps the doubters did not grasp the reverence in which the softly spoken yet inspirational woman from Bray is held.

While her trophy cabinet is overflowing with gold medals and world title belts, perhaps her greatest legacy is leaving women's boxing in a vastly better place than she found it - that Serrano trilogy lifting women's boxing to new heights.

Taylor broke through the barriers with a grace which belied the obstacles she faced yet her quiet determination and humble nature will serve as an example of what can be achieved by belief, hard work and a refusal to accept her lot as young girls can now walk the path she laid.

Fierce inside the ring yet unassuming outside of it - even factoring in an impulse-buy speedboat, since sold - superlatives such as trailblazer, icon and Ireland's greatest sportsperson are not hyperbolic, for Taylor's status as a legend is in no way cliched.

She has indicated she will remain in the sport, but for now, there is time to savour an extraordinary career, with her place among boxing's greats set in stone.

Irish boxing is going to be a lesser place.

"I'm retired now so I can eat what I want, but I'm just going to enjoy a nice celebration and look back on a dream ending to a dream career.

"My story is the story of everyone in this room: we all have our ups and downs. I think people resonate with your vulnerabilities and your successes - saw me cope with the heartbreak of Rio, the Chantelle Cameron loss and personal difficulties.

"My story is the story of everyone in this room."

fullText:
NEW YORK — It's probably fitting that in the world's economic and marketing capital, a Grand Slam tennis tournament doubles as one giant product-placement opportunity.

Little-known players who play on stadium courts end up with last-minute patches stuck onto their kits. Their lesser-known coaches wear hats from brands such as the IT company Infosys and the used-car retailer Carvana.

The week before the U.S. Open is a strange mélange of tennis-related activations. Aryna Sabalenka appears at a Brooklyn Heights pizza joint to promote an energy drink. The Waldorf Astoria puts a tennis court in its famed ballroom for an exhibition with Tommy Paul, Maria Sakkari, Ben Shelton and Leylah Fernandez to promote its new global racquet club venture. Jannik Sinner, injured and back home, chimes in from afar on social media, saying he misses everyone at the U.S. Open, including "@baccarathotels and the whole team who always makes me feel at home."

As the field gets winnowed down and all but the biggest stars and some supporting characters remain, there's a pretty good chance tennis fans might scratch their heads and wonder why so many coaches are wearing swag with one of two or three ubiquitous logos.

One of the most prominent is Eight Sleep.

The company makes high-tech mattress covers that users can heat or cool to their desired temperature. The product tracks sleep patterns and measures users' quality of rest. It is not to be confused with IM8, the nutritional supplement company co-founded by David Beckham.

IM8 has Sabalenka as an ambassador. Her coaching staff has worn IM8 swag, though things can get confusing because her coach, Anton Dubrov, is now part of the Eight Sleep team.

Sabalenka, the two-time reigning champion and world No. 1, plays most of her matches in Arthur Ashe Stadium and many of those in primetime. The camera often shifts to her coaching box. That's a lot of airtime for Eight Sleep, even though Sabalenka does not directly endorse the company.

Dubrov does. So does Frédéric Fontang, who coaches Jiří Lehečka, and Michael Russell, who coaches Taylor Fritz, and Jamie Delgado, who coaches Grigor Dimitrov.

On Russell, the logo for Eight Sleep has to fight for attention, since Russell is the closest thing tennis coaching has to a NASCAR driver. He wears patches from Waterdrop and Solinco. Hats from Eight Sleep and Papatui, a men's skincare brand founded by Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson. Sometimes, Russell wears a Carvana shirt.

Carvana is another of the logos that are everywhere at this U.S. Open — it's on the coaching teams of Amanda Anisimova, Madison Keys and many more.

Alexandra Zatarain, a co-founder of Eight Sleep, said the company has worked with athletes, including Fritz, but these days it often makes more sense to work with their coaches.

They are the ones who set a player's routine, working with a nutritionist on what they eat, and with a physiotherapist and fitness trainer to plan the athlete's preparation and recovery, practices that have become far more complex over the last decade. Optimizing sleep is a big part of that.

"We had this idea of just, 'Oh, what if we make the coaches our partners because they are actually a really important partner in making sure that the player stays on track in terms of all of their health,'" Zatarain said.

And, fortuitously for would-be sponsors, something happened in tennis that made these arrangements even more appealing. Coaches are allowed to coach more openly. They don't have to speak with hidden signals, like removing a hat when they want a player to serve wide or standing and clapping when they want the player to move closer to the net.

In 2022, the U.S. Open launched a trial that allowed off-court coaching during matches for the first time. The other Grand Slams followed the next year. In 2025, World Tennis, the sport's world governing body, changed the rules, allowing it essentially everywhere.

The interplay between players and their coaches often generates some of the most dramatic viewing moments of a tennis match. So, the camera finds them — a lot.

"The coaches, I think, are getting a little bit more visibility," Zatarain said.

Their jobs have also changed in recent years, as teams have grown and coaching a top player has become a sophisticated operation. In the best and most serious environments, it's something like being a chief operating officer of a Formula 1 team, where the player is the car.

Enter the relationships with companies that seek to improve the health of people who may or may not compete in sports. There are only so many tennis players who care about what kind of strings a coach and player might prefer. But everybody sleeps. And a lot of people take energy supplements, including just about every player on tour.

"It's like a holistic approach," Fontang said,  "with clear goals, a clear process and to something that you do consistently right as well in the process. This is how you bring consistency into the match."

Fontang played on the tour in the 1990s, which is now considered a prehistoric era in terms of recovery science. He did a little stretching and mobility work before and after he played. Occasionally, he might get attention from a tour trainer or physiotherapist. He certainly didn't have one on his team.

Ivan Lendl, a star of the 1980s, was the first major men's player known to focus on health and wellness. Martina Navratilova was the first woman.

They both won a lot. Other players noticed.

Now, everything is tracked. Blood gets tested to monitor training and recovery. Nearly everyone rides a stationary bike — high tension, low speed — after a match and quickly downs a protein recovery drink.

And therein lies the opportunity. What separates the Eight Sleeps and IM8s and Solincos of the world is that they have an actual use in the sport, compared with a random resort company that just uses a coach as a billboard. A couple of years ago, Fritz had Eight Sleep install a mattress pad in his hotel room in New York.

Nearly every player goes through a sophisticated recovery routine, but the common denominator is the most valuable recovery activity of all.

"Sleep is the first thing that is the most important," Dubrov said after a late match — a common occurrence at the U.S. Open. Everything else will get cut short so that Sabalenka can maximize the amount of time she can spend in bed, though quality can count as much as quantity.

The hot European summer was not great. There isn't much air conditioning in London homes.

"You can have like 10 hours of the sleep," Dubrov said. "But you're going to be kind of awake for most of it."

Russell said he was introduced to Eight Sleep by Fritz, who has long had sleep issues because he can spend a lot of time playing video games. As a teenager, he got in trouble with USTA coaches because he was often gaming until 4 a.m. It's healthier than clubbing, but still not great.

His team noticed improvements in his sleep data in recent years. Maybe it's his mattress pad. Maybe it's a placebo effect, which Russell calls "the most powerful drug there is."

And a clear branding opportunity, present even as Fritz lost Saturday in five sets to Argentina's Francisco Cerúndolo.

So, no matter who advances to the second week of this marquee tournament, expect plenty more sponsorship and caps that look like they could be plentiful at company retreats.

title: Jorrel Hato Issues 'Dangerous' Warning To Arsenal As Chelsea Eye Premier League Win
description: Chelsea are heading into the London derby full of confidence after back-to-back Premier League wins.
fullText:
Previewing Chelsea's Premier League clash against Arsenal.

Jorrel Hato is relishing Chelsea's Premier League clash against Arsenal on Sunday afternoon.

Chelsea head to the Emirates to face the current champions, looking to end a run of four straight away league defeats to Mikel Arteta's side.

After his summer appointment, Xabi Alonso is hoping to claim a first away league win against the Gunners since 2021, when Chelsea claimed a 2-0 victory.

It's been a positive start to Chelsea's campaign, with wins over Fulham and Brighton and Hove Albion in their opening league matches. Hato has started both league games, with the summer arrival Pep Chavarria still settling into his new surroundings in west London.

The 20-year-old will be keen to keep his place in the side with a start against Arsenal.

Chelsea's toughest test of the season awaits. Their record against the so-called 'big six' away from home has been problematic in recent years.

Whether they're ready to be title challengers yet remains to be seen and that will be established in the coming months. But given the recruitment and start the Blues have made, they are certainly heading in a positive direction.

A win at the Emirates would not only continue the perfect start to the season in terms of points, making it three wins from three, it would signify a statement of intent and sign of change, as they overcome their biggest hurdle - not losing against the Gunners, who they used to have so much joy against.

The squad are looking forward to the London derby. They've been dangerous in attack, scoring seven goals in their opening two games, aided by the trio of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro.

But defensively, they have also been open. Five goals conceded already and if there is any team who will look to punish errors or any openings, it is Arsenal.

That's the aim for Chelsea. To show improvement against Arsenal, and if they can manage a clean sheet - that is a huge bonus.

Arsenal are yet to concede this season, so Chelsea will have their work cut out. Patience and ruthlessness in box boxes will be key.

Preparations are almost done, and Hato has warned Arsenal of the danger Chelsea will pose.

Previewing the trip to the Emirates, Hato told the club's in-house media: "We look at things game by game. I think we had a great start. We spoke with each other and said: 'Okay, the first week, three games has to be three wins,' and we did that. So now we're looking forward to Arsenal.

"I can't see the future, but we try to improve to not concede three goals, but we know we are very dangerous up front, that we will score goals.

"I think against Arsenal is a good test, but I think it was against Fulham and Brighton as well. They are both great teams and we won those games, so we are looking forward to the next one now."

It won't define Chelsea's season if they lose. But if they win, the belief of the squad will exponentially grow, knowing they've managed to overcome a huge hurdle so early into the season.

The South Korean will now miss the trip to Perth on Wednesday night to take on St Johnstone, plus double header against the Rangers, as well as the Europa League opener against Ferencvaros, something that will be a blow to Martin O'Neill as Yang has become one of his key assets.

It's not only the South Korean's trickery on the flanks that's impressive, he also knows his way to goal, with his strike against the Buddies being his second in as many games, following on from finding the back of the net against Aberdeen at Celtic Park last Wednesday night.

Yang seems to have excelled under the guidance of Martin O'Neill, and it's no surprise that his upcoming absence due to international duty is seen as a massive blow to both the Celtic manager and supporters alike.

That in itself illustrates how much the 24 year old has improved under the veteran Irishman, as only a year ago most of us wouldn't have been too concerned  if the South Korean international was omitted from the side.

title: Badiashile suffers nightmare Napoli debut as Chelsea loanee slammed: ‘His fault’
description: Chelsea loanee Benoît Badiashile received low ratings from Italian sports papers following Napoli’s 3-2 loss against Inter, with the French centre-back blamed for two of the Nerazzurri’s goals.N...
fullText:
Chelsea loanee Benoît Badiashile received low ratings from Italian sports papers following Napoli's 3-2 loss against Inter, with the French centre-back blamed for two of the Nerazzurri's goals.

Napoli wasted a two-goal lead in their away game against Inter on Saturday, suffering their second consecutive loss in Serie A.

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Marcus Thuram of Internazionale celebrates scoring his team's second goal during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

Chelsea loanee Badiashile made his Serie A debut coming off the bench in the final ten minutes, with the Partenopei leading 2-1, but his impact was beyond negative.

Inter striker Thuram overjumped him to score Inter's equaliser, but the Napoli defender was also blamed for the Nerazzurri's winner, scored by Lautaro Martinez in stoppage time.

Football Italia rated Badiashile 5/10, the same mark he received from Gazzetta dello Sport and Tuttosport.

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of Napoli, reacts during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Gazzetta blamed Badiashile for Inter's second goal, but also criticised Massimiliano Allegri for introducing the Chelsea loanee: "Badiashile lost Thuram, who headed home the equaliser," the pink paper wrote.

"It was his fault, but also the fault of whoever decided to bring on a new defender who hadn't played in ages at the most crucial moment."

Corriere dello Sport was even harsher on Badiashile, rating him 4.5/10: "He hadn't played since March 7, and he showed. Thuram outjumped him for the header, and he was also partly at fault for the third goal."

LONDON, ENGLAND – JANUARY 31: Benoit Badiashile of Chelsea reacts during the Premier League match between Chelsea and West Ham United at Stamford Bridge on January 31, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Badiashile joined Napoli on a paid €3m loan deal from Chelsea this summer. The Partenopei have an option to make his move permanent for €27m at the end of the season.

Napoli's next game is against Arsenal at the Stadio Maradona next Wednesday, in their 2026-27 Champions League opener.

title: Blades owners speak - but many questions remain
description: BBC Radio Sheffield's Rob Staton reflects on a podcast appearance by Sheffield United owner Steve Rosen - but says questions remain unanswered.
fullText:
"Steve, we've known each other a long time."

And there begins the first long-form interview by anyone involved in Sheffield United's current ownership.

Nathan Zegura, a summariser known as 'the voice' of the Cleveland Browns, is the man sat across from Steve Rosen, the co-chairman at Bramall Lane. They appear to be friends.

It's the kind of conversation that would have been really welcome at the start of Rosen's tenure at United. A warm 'get to know you' piece.

It's not appropriate now though, 18 months into what has been a chaotic period of ownership.

They gave manager Chris Wilder a new contract in January 2025, only to part ways months later.

They then had to go cap in hand back to Wilder after his replacement Ruben Selles lost every game in a disastrous short spell in charge.

This all came after working with pro-gambler James Bord as an advisor, who months later would fail in a bid to buy city rivals Sheffield Wednesday, after squandering money on a list of bad signings.

Maybe things would settle down after that? Nope.

This summer we've had the former owners, United World, claiming they're owed £35m as part of the sale.

This has never been disputed. The holding company that originally controlled United has been liquidated.

Questions remain how the current owners intend to handle the situation, and what actions the English Football League (EFL) and Independent Football Regulator (IFR) will take, if any, following a truly bizarre set of circumstances.

None of these matters are properly addressed in this long-awaited interview. They are airily discussed as if it's merely part of the rough and tumble of running a club.

Every statement on the United World situation and the threat of a possible points deduction has been dismissive, more or less saying it's a storm in a tea cup. There was more of that here.

This is the exchange between Rosen and Negura on the matter:

Rosen: "I can't see in any scenario where the club gets a points deduction because of the (EFL's) insolvency rule. It wasn't like Sheffield Wednesday where they had an administrator and it went into insolvency, couldn't pay their bills and all that. That's not our situation."

Rosen: "Yeah, really good, right?"

Negura: "Because all this is all about winning. Yeah?"

Rosen: "(It's) all about winning."

This isn't an adequate addressing of a significant worry for many fans. We simply don't know yet what the EFL or IFR will do, either, irrespective of what's said here.

To be fair, others have welcomed the opportunity to hear from Rosen. They've even suggested he comes across well. I don't disagree. He's a good talker. He's definitely not an uninteresting person.

But now is not the time to gloss over the big issues off the pitch. It isn't the time to speak about a desire to create United's version of the 'Dawg Pound' - a section of the Cleveland Browns' stadium where fans dress up in costumes and paint their faces.

The last thing we need at Bramall Lane is the Kop turning into a Jack Sparrow convention in honour of Captain Blade.

Neither did it feel appropriate to ask for an explanation on what relegation is. Die-hard Blades have waited ages to hear from the men at the top of their club and when they finally get something, this is what they're subjected to?

The whole thing felt like a safe means to end accusations that the owners never speak - but does this really count? A podcast chat with a mate, skirting around the big issues with a smile?

There are still serious questions to be asked and clarity to be delivered. Neither Rosen nor his co-chairman Helmy Eltoukhy have spoken to the Sheffield media since buying the club.

The invitation is still very much open. The fans deserve it, because we'll be willing to ask the questions that need to be asked. The owners should also be expected to come up with convincing answers under pressure.

fullText:
We've all seen it. A college football game is coming to its inevitable end. And as is so often the case, there's going to be a winner, there's going to be a loser, and everyone watching knows who the latter will be. The cameras pan to the coach of the soon to be losing team. He stares into the middle distance, contemplating decisions made and actions taken, questioning his strategy, his tactics, and his very worth as a coach of football and a leader of young men.

"Lou Holtz's chartreuse Maserati!" you exclaim. "What must that poor sap be thinking right now?"

Ladies and gentlemen, this is Tennessee State head coach Reggie Barlow gamely facing the media following his team's 63-3 loss to Georgia.

I ask you: what was Reggie Barlow thinking?

a) "Look, they were going to beat the ever-loving stew out of somebody in week one. Might as well be us."

b) "Wait, they really gained 611 yards of offense? I saw that on the stat sheet and just assumed I was hallucinating from the heat."

c) "Hey, we decided to start the season against a truly elite national program. But only because Clemson was already spoken for."

d) "I feel bad that I shrieked and jumped under the desk when the guy from the Bogart Biweekly called my name. But he looked a little like Raylen Wilson and I didn't want to take any chances."

fullText:
Borussia Mönchengladbach have endured a miserable start to the Bundesliga season, picking up zero points from their opening two games.

After being beaten 3-0 by RB Leipzig in their opener, Die Fohlen looked on course for their first win when they raced into a 3-1 lead against SV Elversberg at Borussia-Park on Saturday.

However, they completely let the game slip away, eventually suffering a dramatic 4-3 defeat.

Speaking to ZDF after the game, Gladbach captain Tim Kleindienst was furious with the mistakes and lapses in concentration that allowed Elversberg back into the match.

"We need to raise our level of focus as quickly as possible so that it lasts for 90 minutes. And I have no idea what the reason is – maybe watch less TikTok or whatever. I honestly don't care what they do," Kleindienst said, delivering a blunt message to his teammates.

"At the end of the day, they just need to do something so that they stay clear-headed for 90 minutes, make it through the full 90 minutes, and keep their focus so that we can defend until the very end. And not keep giving the ball away needlessly, making misplaced passes and committing fouls."

title: “Outrageous and Indefensible”: Skip Bayless Fumes as Michigan Secure Hail Mary Win Over Western Michigan
description: The Michigan Wolverines’ season opener against the Western Michigan Broncos ended in the most dramatic way possible. Western Michigan looked to have sealed a remarkable upset when Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood’s Hail Mary attempt landed out of bounds as time expired.
fullText:
The Michigan Wolverines' season opener against the Western Michigan Broncos ended in the most dramatic way possible.

Western Michigan looked to have sealed a remarkable upset when Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood's Hail Mary attempt landed out of bounds as time expired. However, despite TV replays showing that the clock had hit zero before the ball hit a Western Michigan defender, officials put a second back on the clock, giving the Wolverines one more play. This time, Underwood connected with wide receiver JJ Buchanan for a 47-yard score, sealing a controversial win.

Sports analyst Skip Bayless said it was unfair that the Wolverines were awarded one more play to score.

"Giving Michigan one more play just might've been the most outrageous and indefensible home cooking I've ever witnessed," Bayless wrote.

Underwood led the charge with a touchdown and 170 passing yards as Michigan chalked up its first win of the year in dramatic fashion.

Even though Skip Bayless called out the manner of the Michigan Wolverines' victory, he was still glad about the result. In another post on X/Twitter, Bayless said that as an Oklahoma Sooners fan, he'd rather they face the Wolverines after a win than a loss.

"As an Oklahoma fan, I'm glad Michigan managed to pull out its first game under Kyle Whittingham. Would not have wanted my Sooners going up to Ann Arbor next Saturday with the Wolverines seething after a home loss to Western Michigan," Bayless shared.

Brent Venables' Sooners are scheduled to face Kyle Whittingham's Wolverines on Saturday, Sept. 12.

title: How McLaren left itself exposed at the F1 Italian Grand Prix
description: McLaren's qualifying slip-ups at Formula 1's Italian Grand Prix masked encouraging performance on what was supposed to be a tough track for the team
fullText:
As Pierre Gasly and Alpine mastered the qualifying game to perfection at Monza, McLaren was one of several Formula 1 teams wondering what could have been after several key factors led to an underwhelming Italian Grand Prix qualifying result.

Off the back of two wins at high downforce circuits in Budapest and Zandvoort, high-speed Monza was never expected to be McLaren's strongest track, both because of a slightly less aero efficient car and a known weakness in low-speed chicanes.

In fact, team principal Andrea Stella called the Temple of Speed a good test to see if McLaren's progress was able to carry over on different track layouts. Looking at Q2, the MCL40 looked set to pass that test with flying colours, with Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris second and third behind Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli.

But, like several other frontrunners, McLaren couldn't replicate that form in Q3. Piastri only found a tenth on his first Q3 run, while Norris was exposed by Piastri's off at Turn 1, robbing him of a crucial slipstream from his team-mate.

As Gasly's shock pole in the Alpine showed, execution was everything, ranging from battery and tyre management to on-track positioning on the outlap to find the perfect tow. That's where Mercedes' George Russell lost pole as he was too close behind a cunning Max Verstappen and, according to Stella, his team's Q3 execution also cost it a better result than third for Piastri and a lowly ninth for Norris.

"When we executed well, like in Q2, we had the two cars P1, P2, then they ended up P2, P3 at the end of Q2, because the cars were positioned in the right place in terms of slipstream, and both Oscar and Lando drove the cars very well despite the small gaps to the cars ahead," Stella explained.

"[In Q3] on the first attempt probably Lando had too big a gap to the car ahead, he lost some time in some corners. So, in terms of execution we leave some performance behind, while Oscar did a very good lap. Then, in the final run, we had some issues managing the battery, and here in Monza every percent of battery charge costs you a significant amount of milliseconds. And then we had the issue with Oscar locking in corner 1. So overall, there are multiple areas in which we have not executed at the level that we should have."

One mitigating factor, though Stella was keen not to call it in as an excuse, was McLaren's garage position at the end of the pitlane. That heavily encouraged the McLarens to go out first for the final run, because if they had waited for others they were at risk of getting blocked leaving their pit box by a train of cars in the fast lane. That would relegate them to the tail end of the field, with a chance of not being able to start the final attempt before the clock runs out.

As it was, Piastri and Norris were first in the train with no other cars to collect a slipstream from ahead of them. With the Australian then missing his braking point into Turn 1, it left Norris all exposed.

"At no point should this be an excuse, but when you are at the first garage, you need to be a little bit careful in leaving the garage too late, because if you are the last one, there's a risk that then you're not going to be in time opening the lap," Stella explained. "So that's also why we found ourselves being first, but probably we have to review the margins that we adopted, because then being first with the slipstream effect that we have this year seems definitely a position that you don't want to be."

Piastri's lock-up in Turn 1, hurting his team-mate in the process, sent the internet's conspiracy theorists into a frenzy, though both he and Norris had been struggling with front-tyre locking into the chicane all day. F1's 2026 battery management needs on energy-starved Monza made it tough for drivers to work heat into their brakes, Stella explained, because they couldn't afford to deviate from their optimal energy harvesting strategy.

"It's very specific to Monza," the Italian said. "There's not much energy that you can spend in an outlap to properly work your brakes, because the harvest is so limited that you need to pay a lot of attention to it. It's not like you can do lots of acceleration and braking, warm up your brakes, plus if you start to do so, you may lose contact with the car ahead, so it's very tricky.

"That's certainly something that we might have to look into in terms of making sure that the brakes can operate even without this input of energy that you have to give in outlaps, but I would say that the problem here is very much Monza-specific."

Overall, Stella felt the team's underlying performance was encouraging for other low-draw circuits on the calendar and said its lack of aero efficiency was a "red herring" given the improvements the team had made to the car, including the introduction of its rotating rear wing design.

If Monza was an exam for the overall performance of the MCL40, Stella gave his team a half pass. "Our engineers have done a good job of minimising drag, and once we also optimised the power unit and the energy management, we were actually not that far off in terms of top speed. It would be a little bit of a red herring or an excuse to say we have too much drag.

"I think if we had done a better job of execution and controlling some parameters that don't only depend on the pure performance of the car, we could have definitely qualified on the first couple of rows on the grid. So, it's almost a half pass from a performance point of view in terms of Monza being an exam."

title: Ira Winderman: Heat at top of East or play-in? It’s a very fine line.
description: MIAMI — The prevailing notion once LeBron James put pen to paper on July 27 was that the stage was set in the Eastern Conference, that assessments could be set when it came to standings, seedings. Yes, there was some cleanup work around the conference in the interim, most notably the Cavaliers’ acquisition of Peyton Watson, but otherwise mostly ancillary stuff, like the 76ers adding Kentavious ...
fullText:
MIAMI — The prevailing notion once LeBron James put pen to paper on July 27 was that the stage was set in the Eastern Conference, that assessments could be set when it came to standings, seedings.

Yes, there was some cleanup work around the conference in the interim, most notably the Cavaliers' acquisition of Peyton Watson, but otherwise mostly ancillary stuff, like the 76ers adding Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Charlotte adding Dennis Schroder, and the Heat signing Klay Thompson and Nick Richards.

And then came Kawhi Day on Wednesday, in all its NBA drama in regard to the death penalties delivered to the Los Angeles Clippers.

Because with that finality, it meant that Kawhi Leonard to the Raptors again was a thing, an East acquisition on a level somewhere between Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Heat and Jaylen Brown to the 76ers.

So, no, we weren't done with the LeBron-a-thon resetting the East.

But now we seemingly should be.

Because the Raptors are for real, perhaps as for real as when Leonard last was in the team's colors, during that run to the 2019 title.

So now, and only now, can stock truly be taken of where Pat Riley's massive Miami makeover has left the Heat in a conference upgraded with significant talent, what with both LeBron and Kawhi coming East.

At the moment, FanDuel lists 10 Eastern Conference teams with projected winning records, which also is the limit for postseason spots (when counting the four play-in seeds).

From that list, FanDuel has the Heat tied with the Raptors for the sixth and final direct entry to the playoffs, as the No. 6 seed, at 45 1/2 wins.

So Heat play-in for a fifth consecutive season?

Or ready to challenge not only for direct entry into the playoffs, but potentially even homecourt in the first round?

But at least now, with Kawhi resolution, cases can be made in earnest.

Considering the Pistons won the East last season at 60-22, projecting the conference's best at 52 1/2 wins speaks volumes about the competition in the East.

Last season's championship had a lightning-in-a-bottle feel, with New York City seemingly celebrating as such.

Subbing in Andre Drummond for Mitchell Robinson is a downgrade, which could lead to a downturn from the Knicks' 53 victories last season.

This is not like chasing the Thunder at the top of the West.

The top seed in the East is there for the taking.

In light of the Jaylen Brown trade, it's almost as if the Celtics are being viewed as top two in the East based on reputation.

For all the power tandems in the East, who exactly stands as second-best Celtic to Jayson Tatum? Derrick White? Paul George?

And for all the doubts about the Heat's depth, it's not exactly as if the Celtics are rolling out starting-level talent off their bench, with all due respect to Sam Hauser, Hugo Gonzalez and Baylor Scheierman.

Tobias Harris out and John Collins in. Is that necessarily an upgrade? And don't discount the loss of Isaiah Stewart and his incredible bulk.

Yes, there were gains in the margins with the additions of Isaiah Joe, Gary Harris and Taurean Prince, but there remains the question of one-year wonder or something more from the Pistons.

The addition of Peyton Watson is meaningful, but consider also how it came at the cost of Max Strus, Dean Wade and Dennis Schroder.

After consecutive playoff flameouts, is the motivation still there?

Any time a team puts this much stock into James Harden, doubts are reasonable.

Is it fantasy (as in stats) or reality when it comes to this much talent in a single lineup?

The usage rate with Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, Anfernee Simons and VJ Edgecombe seemingly would require at least 1 1/2 balls in play to sate all six based on last season's numbers.

Something has to give. The talent is there, but it is a huge sum of a lot of parts for Nick Nurse to manage.

When it comes to measuring up to the Heat, you could start here: Which duo is better – Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo for the Heat or Leonard and Scottie Barnes for the Raptors? Taking either side would be by the slimmest of margins.

Then, looking at the remainder of the Raptors' roster, a case that with the likes of RJ Barrett, Immanuel Quickley, Ja'Kobe Walter, Jakob Poeltl and Collin Murray-Broyles, there is depth that measures up to the Heat.

The games between the teams have always been close … so could this season's final record.

As mentioned above with the example with the Raptors, where does Antetokounmpo-Adebayo stand in the East? On par with Toronto's Leonard-Barnes, the Knicks' Jalen Brunson-Karl-Anthony Towns, the Celtics' Tatum-White, the Pistons' Cade Cunningham-Jalen Duren, the Cavaliers' Donovan Mitchell-Harden, or any 76ers two-man group?

Otherwise, the Heat's supporting case seemingly is being sold short by most, when considering the presence of Andrew Wiggins, Davion Mitchell, Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr., Klay Thompson and Pelle Larsson, to name a half-dozen supporting players.

Did we mention that Tyrese Haliburton is back? Or that Ivica Zubac is about to start his first full season with the Pacers?

And there still are Pascal Siakam, Aaron Nesmith, Obi Toppin, Andrew Nembhard, T.J. McConnell, plus the addition of Kelly Oubre.

Remember, two seasons ago the Pacers were a 50-win team and in the NBA Finals.

Yes, the team that went 5-0 last season against the Heat, with a returning core, is ranked below.

With Nikola Vucevic in for Moe Wagner, the Magic will stand as Exhibit A of how much a coaching change, alone, can change a culture.

It was an offseason of quality gained (Devin Carter, Lu Dort, Ryan Nembhard and Aaron Wiggins) and little of contribution lost (Jonathan Kuminga, Zaccharie Risacher).

It likely will come down to whether a defensive-driven roster can find enough scoring beyond Jalen Johnson. If Atlanta does, the win total could far exceed expectations.

title: Katie Taylor bows out as three-time undisputed champion
description: Katie Taylor brought her remarkable boxing career to a close in front of 80,000 jubilant fans at Croke Park, bowing out as a three-time undisputed world champion.The Bray native produced a dominant pe...
fullText:
Katie Taylor brought her remarkable boxing career to a close in front of 80,000 jubilant fans at Croke Park, bowing out as a three-time undisputed world champion.

The Bray native produced a dominant performance against unbeaten Flora Pili, securing a points victory to claim the vacant WBC light-welterweight title and complete an extraordinary final chapter.

Taylor finishes her career with 26 victories from 27 professional contests, having established herself as one of Ireland's greatest sporting figures.

The 40-year-old's farewell in Dublin was a night of celebration, spectacle and music, with Croke Park providing a fitting stage for the final appearance of a fighter who has transformed women's boxing.

And among the many supporters celebrating Taylor's achievements were Leeds United fans, with the former Republic of Ireland footballer having long spoken about her affection for the Whites.

Appearing on Soccer AM in 2019, Taylor revealed the origins of her Leeds connection.

"My team is actually Leeds United.

"My dad is from Leeds and my older two brothers grew up supporting Leeds as well. Every Christmas we would get Leeds jerseys for Christmas and football boots. I was a huge football fan growing up."

Taylor has previously described her visits to Elland Road as "some of my best memories as a kid", while her love of the club has remained throughout her hugely successful boxing career.

That connection was strengthened in 2021 when Taylor brought her world championship belts to Leeds, successfully defending her titles against Jennifer Han at Headingley Stadium.

Now, five years on from her night in Leeds, Taylor has called time on a career which saw her become a three-time undisputed world champion and one of the most influential figures in the history of women's sport.

Her final victory over Pili ensured she departed the sport on her own terms, adding another world title to a glittering collection before receiving the farewell she deserved in front of 80,000 fans at Croke Park.

From the football pitches of Ireland to the biggest stages in boxing, Taylor's journey has been extraordinary.

And for Leeds United supporters, she will always be remembered as one of their own.

title: “Absolutely Robbed”: CFB Fans Feel For Western Michigan as Wolverines Win Low Scoring Thriller on Hail Mary
description: The Western Michigan Broncos almost pulled off an upset victory over the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday. A low-scoring game in Ann Arbor left fans on the edge of their seats.
fullText:
The Western Michigan Broncos almost pulled off an upset victory over the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday. A low-scoring game in Ann Arbor left fans on the edge of their seats.

In the fourth quarter, Western Michigan looked set for a huge upset after two field goals by Dieter Kelly. However, just before the final whistle, Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood's Hail Mary attempt connected with wide receiver JJ Buchanan.

The clock appeared to have expired before the quarterback's previous throw. However, the officials put one second back after review, ruling that it touched an out-of-bounds Western Michigan defender. Underwood then connected with Buchanan for a 47-yard touchdown to seal the win.

After the game, fans on social media reacted to Michigan's thrilling victory and Western Michigan's loss.

"Absolutely robbed," one fan wrote.

title: Texas A&M looks to end its College GameDay struggles in 2026

Texas A&M kicked off the 2026 regular season against Missouri State on Saturday night, and while starting the season off 1-0 was fully expected, one of third-year coach Mike Elko's remaining challenges that has haunted the program for 20-plus seasons resurfaced this week before the season opener, as ESPN's College GameDay's nine appearances in College Station have been disastrous.

Since 2000, Texas A&M is just 1-8 when College GameDay made its way to College Station, with the first loss coming against No. 1 Oklahoma 35-31, while the only win came during the 2016 season when the Aggies defeated visiting Tennessee 45-38 in double overtime, which happens to be one of the most exciting finishes in recent memory.

Since that victory, the Jimbo Fisher era has been equally disappointing after six seasons, while the lone College GameDay loss to Clemson during Fisher's first season at the helm was a game that could, and should have, gone the other way if it weren't for several avoidable performances.

During Mike Elko's inaugural season, Texas A&M's loss to rival Texas at the end of the 2024 season wasn't a shock given the talent differential, while the Aggies' first-round loss to Miami in the first round of the College Football Playoff was by far the most disappointing defeat with College GameDay in town.

When the lights are brightest, Texas A&M must respond if the Aggies want to be taken seriously as a program truly building and contending for national titles, and while the 2025 season was certainly a solid start, expectations are even higher in 2026. If College GameDay makes its way back to College Station, it's time to change the narrative.

title: Commanders WR has one word to describe offense vs. Eagles in Week 1

fullText:
More than a few young athletes have gone to the NFL, NBA, MLB and talk about what they are going to do. They make it sound easy. You know why? Because they think it will be easier than it will be. They have not yet gained enough professional experience to understand how much more competitive things are professionally.

That might be the case with Washington Commanders' receiver/punt returner Jaylin Lane. Oh, he has exhibited a very sincere nature. He seems like a genuine young man. So he certainly has good intentions. But he did tell Scott Abraham this week, "I just think how we attack every day at practice. At the end of the day, this is the only sport where you practice more than you play."

Uh oh, Lane apparently has no idea how many hours swimmers spend in the pool each week, much more than during a swim meet. There's not a golfer who made it successfully to the PGA Tour that didn't spend hundreds of hours on the range, working on their short game, finally to have the opportunity to play in a tournament.

"Your days at practice leading up to the game, they got to be really good. And I think this is a really good week for us because yesterday we had a great day. Today we came out and attacked. So I think we are just, you know, ramping up to get ready."

I caught up with Commanders second year WR Jaylin Lane after today's practice.

About the David Blough offense that will be unleashed against the Eagles, Jaylin told me, "it's going to be explosive...I'm excited." pic.twitter.com/L7s9Ax5ZBk

When Abraham asked, "What is this offense going to be like?" Lane quickly responded, "Yeah, it's going to be explosive! We got a lot of explosive guys on the field. And Blough and the rest of the offensive side, they've been putting us in great positions to use our explosiveness. So, expect an explosive offense. I'm excited."

I'm glad Lane is excited; I'm glad he really likes OC David Blough's offense and coaching. I hope he's up to the challenge of NFL defenses. In the Commanders' first game, the offense will face the Eagles' defense. In the third week, they will face the Seahawks defense, which led Seattle to a Super Bowl Championship in 2025.

Hope Lane can have his own success this season.

title: Bill Madden: Tampa Bay Rays ready to usher in new era with stadium relocation near
description: NEW YORK — For years baseball people have marveled at the Tampa Bay Rays’ ability to remain competitive in the American League East despite consistently low industry payrolls and annual attendance. fullText:
NEW YORK — For years baseball people have marveled at the Tampa Bay Rays' ability to remain competitive in the American League East despite consistently low industry payrolls and annual attendance. Since 2008, the Rays have been to the postseason nine times, including the World Series twice, always with payrolls of well over $100 million less than the Yankees.

At the same time, Tampa Bay fans have gotten used to the Rays' jettisoning their favorite players (See: Isaac Paredes, Randy Arozarena, Brandon Lowe and Tyler Glasnow in just the last three years) as soon as they became too costly or near free agency. And with the clock continuing to tick on their expiring (2028) lease at dreary Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla., there's never been a sense of permanence of the Rays in Tampa Bay.

Recently, both the Tampa city council and the Hillsborough County commissioners voted to approve a new $2.3 billion mixed-use stadium project near Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry Boulevard campus, not far from Raymond James Stadium, the home of the NFL Tampa Bay Bucs. The plan is similar to what the Atlanta Braves constructed in Cobb County, Ga., in 2015 for a stadium surrounded by a village of shops and restaurants that would produce addition revenue for the team.

It was always the accepted view of most folks in the Tampa Bay area that if the Rays were going to survive they would have to be in Tampa where the large majority of their 3 1/2 million residents are. This was part of the reason the Rays have remained one of the top revenue sharing recipients in baseball, an average of nearly $60 million a year. That's on top of the $50 million they and the other 29 clubs receive annually from the MLB Central Fund. So they've had the money to increase payroll, but the previous Rays owner Stu Sternberg just chose not to spend it.

If the owners are able to establish a cap in the new collective bargaining agreement, revenue sharing would go away, but the Rays are anticipating revenues of far more than $60 million from the new park and surrounding village which is now slated to be ready by 2029. For sure, now that the stadium issue has finally been resolved, the Rays, under their new ownership led by Jacksonville developer Patrick Zalupski, are expected to be operating vastly different. Last week Zalupski told the Tampa Bay Times: "Tampa's the No. 11 media market in the country. There's nothing holding it back, "adding that with the new ballpark and the development around it, "we should be able to drive payroll (currently 27th at $116,208,358) into the top 15 circle and maybe even the top 10."

In the meantime, the Rays have been leading the American League East since June 27, but will be facing their biggest challenge now in the September stretch, starting with this present road trip through Texas where they snapped a 10-game skid at Globe Life Field as of Friday, and three in Atlanta against the Braves. They then finish the season with three games with the Red Sox, four in New York with the Yankees and three more at home with the Phillies.

That four-game series at Yankee Stadium Sept. 22-24 figures to be the biggest regular-season series for both the Rays and the Yankees in years, especially since the Yankees expect to be (Aaron Judge) whole, while Rays GM Eric Neander made significant upgrades to his pitching at the trade deadline with Freddy Peralta from the Mets and hard-throwing righty reliever Tyler Wells from the Orioles, and in perhaps the best acquisition of all, filled the Rays longstanding need — a catcher who can hit — by landing Liam Hicks from the Marlins

If the Rays are able to emerge through that gauntlet still atop the AL East it should be cause for considerable concern for the Yankees. Because as improved as they've become this year, they figure to be this good and better for years to come with one of the top player development systems in baseball with a half dozen top 100 prospects including outfielders Theo Gillen, Jake Melton and Austin Overn and catcher Caden Bodine, all of whom could be making their debuts at some point next year.

In every way, the baseball future couldn't be brighter in Tampa Bay.
